audit.why: 46.15% over 26 games with EVEN/7-10 difficulty matches the level chart, and the mirror (galio__neeko) already recorded no side or rating change. Left the chart untouched to avoid a mirror conflict.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spike text described the level 6 window without the one thing that decides it: Justice Punch's knockup cancels the Pop Blossom wind-up, and Hero's Entrance shields the target of your burst.
audit.why: Galio E is a knockup (kit flags knockup/dash, 11/10/9/8/7s); Neeko R has a preparation before the leap, so any displacement during it denies the ult. Galio R grants a magic shield to allies in the landing area (Riot text).
audit.corrected: Spike and late text now key the ult to Justice Punch's cooldown and name the Hero's Entrance shield.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1].text claimed Neeko can set the ult up 'W-invisible'. Riot's text for Neeko W is a clone plus a passive third-attack proc — no stealth. Only Inherent Glamour (P) hides the wind-up.
audit.why: Kit file is the authority on names and effects; Neeko's W has no stealth flag and no invisibility in its description. Teaching a player to rely on W invisibility gets them killed mid-channel.
audit.corrected: Replaced with the disguise (P) as the concealment, and added that Justice Punch's knockup cancels the wind-up regardless.

audit.whatIsWrong: Neither layer mentioned that Galio's shields (Shield of Durand W, Hero's Entrance R) absorb the burst window, nor that his knockup denies Neeko's only mobility tool.
audit.why: Both flagged in _missing for this exact matchup; Neeko is a single-rotation burst champion, so a shield on the target is the whole fight.
audit.corrected: Written into late, whys[4], wants.foe[1] and report[5].

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns and dosFull[0].d gave no real numbers for Justice Punch.
audit.why: Kit gives 11/10/9/8/7s. Concrete numbers make the step-up window actionable.
audit.corrected: 11s at rank 1, 7s at rank 5 written into breakdown.cooldowns and dosFull[0].d.

audit.whatIsWrong: tldr called it a 'Free poke lane' while diff is EVEN and the win rate is 46.15%.
audit.why: The headline told the player the opposite of what the data and the rest of the page say.
audit.corrected: tldr now reads as an even lane keyed to Justice Punch.

edits.before: Free poke lane — root-Q every CS attempt and save your R for the river, not the raid boss.
edits.after: Even lane — tax his CS with root-bloom Q, and never ult into a live Justice Punch.

edits.before: His dash knockup — he has no engage while it is down. Until it’s spent, every commit is a coin flip.
edits.after: Justice Punch is his only engage and his cancel on your R — down 11s at rank 1. Commit in that window.

edits.before: - Galio Justice Punch: matchup-defining — His dash knockup — he has no engage while it is down. Step up only on its downtime. - Budget W clone + disguise for emergencies and the R for opportunities — never swap them.
edits.after: - Galio Justice Punch: matchup-defining — 11s at rank 1, 7s at rank 5, and its knockup cancels Pop Blossom, so R only once it is gone. - Budget W clone + disguise for emergencies and the R for opportunities — never swap them.

edits.before: Track Galio’s Justice Punch: His dash knockup — he has no engage while it is down. Forward steps wait for its downtime.
edits.after: Track Justice Punch: its knockup is both his engage and his cancel on your Pop Blossom wind-up. Step up and ult on its downtime.

edits.before: Even window — your Pop Blossom off a landed E is a real all-in, but he can W-taunt or simply tank it through his MR if you mistime it.
edits.after: Even window — Pop Blossom off a landed E is a real all-in, but Justice Punch's knockup cancels the wind-up and his taunt eats what's left.

edits.before: Pop Blossom off a landed E is your cleanest all-in window — set the ult up while disguised or W-invisible so he can't pre-taunt the channel.
edits.after: Pop Blossom off a landed E is your cleanest all-in — disguised, the wind-up is hidden, but Justice Punch's knockup still cancels it, so bait his E first.

edits.before: Time his W taunt to eat your E root and Pop Blossom, halving your combo damage
edits.after: Knock you out of the Pop Blossom wind-up with Justice Punch, then taunt through the root

edits.before: Late game this lane is decided by his global R, not by lane trades. Galio's ultimate flies across the map to peel his carries and, worse for you, it interrupts your Pop Blossom wind-up, so you can't channel a teamfight bomb while he's up. His MR stacking means your single AP rotation does less and less the longer the game runs, so you want to be the one engaging from fog with E + R onto a clustered backline, not dueling him. Treat him as a counter-engage threat: ult only when his R is down or he's already committed his W elsewhere.
edits.after: Late game this lane is decided by his global R, not by lane trades. Hero's Entrance drops on an ally with a magic shield that soaks your whole rotation, and its knockup interrupts your Pop Blossom wind-up, so you can't channel a bomb while it's up on a 140-180s timer. His MR stacking means your single AP rotation does less the longer the game runs, so you want to be the one engaging from fog with E + R onto a clustered backline, not dueling him. Treat him as counter-engage: ult only when his R is down or he's already committed his W elsewhere.

notes: Left the level chart alone: the mirror (galio__neeko) recorded no side or rating change, and the packet chart (Skill/Skill/Galio/Galio/Skill/Skill/Skill) disagrees with both layers on rows 0,1,4,5,6 — but full and content already agree with each other, so any change here would have to be made on both sides at once and would fight the already-audited mirror. Also: Neeko's passive is broken by immobilizing CC, and every piece of CC Galio owns (W taunt, E knockup, R knockup) qualifies — the disguise dies the instant he touches you. That fact appears nowhere in either layer; I could not fit it inside the length band on any existing string without dropping something equally important.
